newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil drifts on IPE standoff, French strike.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil drifts on IPE standoff, French strike.

text.p: NWE gas oil trade was sluggish on Monday with traders cautiously assessing the combined effect of a French oil workers' strike and a continuing standoff between the long and the short on the November IPE delivery.

Activity was virtually paralysed with the market variously bullish on news of a continuing stoppage at French oil refineries and bearish on a statement by AIC that it planned to sell 160,000-190,000 tonnes on the ARA market, traders said.
The statement weighed on sentiment but traders said they had not heard any of the material offered on the market.
The AIC statement added that Cargill, the main long, had failed to take delivery and said the matter was in the IPE's hands. Cargill and the IPE decined to comment.
Benchmark IPE futures slipped 50 cents to $219.75 a tonne a after some weakness in U.S. heating oil.
Traders said there was no market consensus on how the strike was affecting French low sulphur import requirements.
Heating oil cargoes were notionally Dec IPE +$6/7, with Russians at +$2/3. Low sulphur diesel was at Dec IPE +$17/19.
Low sulphur diesel barges were $1 lower at Dec IPE +$12/13.50. Heating oil was Dec IPE +$1.50/2.50.
